results.name: Equiv.sumPiEquivProdPi
results.source_text:
/-- The type of dependent functions on a sum type `ι ⊕ ι'` is equivalent to the type of pairs of
functions on `ι` and on `ι'`. This is a dependent version of `Equiv.sumArrowEquivProdArrow`. -/
@[simps (attr := grind =)]
def sumPiEquivProdPi {ι ι'} (π : ι ⊕ ι' → Type*) :
    (∀ i, π i) ≃ (∀ i, π (inl i)) × ∀ i', π (inr i') where
  toFun f := ⟨fun i => f (inl i), fun i' => f (inr i')⟩
  invFun g := Sum.rec g.1 g.2
  left_inv f := by ext (i | i) <;> rfl
results.docstring:
The type of dependent functions on a sum type `ι ⊕ ι'` is equivalent to the type of pairs of
functions on `ι` and on `ι'`. This is a dependent version of `Equiv.sumArrowEquivProdArrow`.

results.name: Fintype.sum_equiv
results.source_text:
@[to_additive /-- `Fintype.sum_equiv` is a specialization of `Finset.sum_bij` that
automatically fills in most arguments.

See `Equiv.sum_comp` for a version without `h`. -/]
lemma prod_equiv (e : ι ≃ κ) (f : ι → M) (g : κ → M) (h : ∀ x, f x = g (e x)) :
    ∏ x, f x = ∏ x, g x := prod_bijective _ e.bijective _ _ h

automatically fills in most arguments.

results.name: Equiv.sigmaEquivProd_sigmaCongrRight
results.source_text:
theorem sigmaEquivProd_sigmaCongrRight :
    (sigmaEquivProd α₁ β₁).symm.trans (sigmaCongrRight e)
    = (prodCongrRight e).trans (sigmaEquivProd α₁ β₂).symm := by
  ext ⟨a, b⟩ : 1
  simp only [trans_apply, sigmaCongrRight_apply, prodCongrRight_apply]
  rfl

results.name: TensorSpecies.Tensor.Pure.prodP_apply_finSumFinEquiv
results.source_text:
lemma Pure.prodP_apply_finSumFinEquiv {n1 n2} {c : Fin n1 → C} {c1 : Fin n2 → C}
    (p1 : Pure S c) (p2 : Pure S c1) (i : Fin n1 ⊕ Fin n2) :
    Pure.prodP p1 p2 (finSumFinEquiv i) =
    match i with
    | Sum.inl i => LinearEquiv.cast (R := k) (by simp) (p1 i)
    | Sum.inr i => LinearEquiv.cast (R := k) (by simp) (p2 i) := by
  rw [Pure.prodP]
  match i with
  | Sum.inl i =>
    simp only [finSumFinEquiv_apply_left, LinearEquiv.cast_apply, Fin.addCases_left]
    rfl
  | Sum.inr i =>
    simp only [finSumFinEquiv_apply_right, LinearEquiv.cast_apply, Fin.addCases_right]
    rfl

results.name: Fin.update_snoc_last

/-- Adding an element at the beginning of a tuple and then updating it amounts to adding it
directly. -/
theorem update_snoc_last : update (snoc p x) (last n) z = snoc p z := by
  ext j
  cases j using lastCases <;> simp

/-- The element representing the `1` in `Fin (1 + n + n)`.
  This is then casted to `Fin (2 * n + 1)`. -/
def oddShiftZero : Fin (2 * n + 1) :=
  Fin.cast (odd_shift_eq n) (Fin.castAdd n (Fin.castAdd n 1))

results.name: ZMod.natCast_zmod_val
results.source_text:
/-- So-named because the coercion is `Nat.cast` into `ZMod`. For `Nat.cast` into an arbitrary ring,
see `ZMod.natCast_val`. -/
theorem natCast_zmod_val {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (a : ZMod n) : (a.val : ZMod n) = a := by
  cases n
  · cases NeZero.ne 0 rfl
  · apply Fin.cast_val_eq_self
results.docstring:
So-named because the coercion is `Nat.cast` into `ZMod`. For `Nat.cast` into an arbitrary ring,
see `ZMod.natCast_val`.

results.name: ZMod.val_natCast
results.source_text:
@[simp]
theorem val_natCast (n a : ℕ) : (a : ZMod n).val = a % n := by
  cases n
  · rw [Nat.mod_zero]
    exact Int.natAbs_natCast a
  · apply Fin.val_natCast

results.name: ZMod.val
results.source_text:
/-- `val a` is a natural number defined as:
  - for `a : ZMod 0` it is the absolute value of `a`
  - for `a : ZMod n` with `0 < n` it is the least natural number in the equivalence class

See `ZMod.valMinAbs` for a variant that takes values in the integers.
-/
def val : ∀ {n : ℕ}, ZMod n → ℕ
  | 0 => Int.natAbs
  | n + 1 => ((↑) : Fin (n + 1) → ℕ)
results.docstring:
`val a` is a natural number defined as:
- for `a : ZMod 0` it is the absolute value of `a`
- for `a : ZMod n` with `0 < n` it is the least natural number in the equivalence class

See `ZMod.valMinAbs` for a variant that takes values in the integers.

results.name: ZMod.natCast_val
results.source_text:
@[simp]
theorem natCast_val [NeZero n] (i : ZMod n) : (i.val : R) = cast i :=
  congr_fun (natCast_comp_val R) i

results.name: ZMod.cast
results.source_text:
/-- Cast an integer modulo `n` to another semiring.
This function is a morphism if the characteristic of `R` divides `n`.
See `ZMod.castHom` for a bundled version. -/
def cast : ∀ {n : ℕ}, ZMod n → R
  | 0 => Int.cast
  | _ + 1 => fun i => i.val
results.docstring:
Cast an integer modulo `n` to another semiring.
This function is a morphism if the characteristic of `R` divides `n`.
See `ZMod.castHom` for a bundled version.

@[simp]
lemma natCast_val {n : ℕ} : val n = n := rfl
